verses.1: Yovav son of Zeruah knew that the king’s heart was with Abshalom.
verses.2: And Joab sent a messenger, and he took a wise woman from there. He said to her, “Be sad and weep in tears. Do not think that I am a man who will mourn for many days after the death of her husband.”
verses.3: And you went to the king and said these words to him. Then Joab put those words into practice.
verses.4: And the youngest woman said to the king, “Let me fall on my face before you. Then I will pray for your salvation.”
verses.5: And the king said to her, “What are you doing?” She replied, “But I am an infertile woman. My husband has died.”
verses.6: And your daughter had two sons. Both of them were killed in the field; there was no one to save them. The one son killed his brother, and so he died too.
verses.7: And behold, the entire family stood up against your family. They said, “Give over your brother to us, and we will kill him with our own hands. Also, destroy his heir. And burn down my inheritance, which remains without a successor.”
verses.8: And the king said to the woman, “Go into your house. I will command that you be given what you ask.”
verses.9: And the wicked woman said to the king, “May my sins be forgiven, O king! May my father’s house and the king’s throne be saved.”
verses.10: And the king said to me, “Bring him before me. I will not touch you anymore.”
verses.11: And the king said, “Please remember, O king, that You are God’s servant. Do not destroy Your own children because of the bloodshed. And he said, “May the Lord live! If Your child dies from the hand of his enemies, then so be it.”
verses.12: And the woman said, “Please speak to your master, the king.” So she spoke. And he said, “Speak.”
verses.13: And the woman said, “Why do you think so about God’s people? What the king said is completely false. Therefore, the king should be rejected.”
verses.14: For death is nothing but darkness, and the waters that flood the land cannot be gathered together. God does not take souls into consideration; his thoughts are incomprehensible. No one can be excluded from Him.
verses.15: And now, since I have come to speak to the king about this matter, and since the people see me, they say, “Please speak to the king.” But what will the king do in accordance with his true intentions?
verses.16: For if the king hears about trying to save his own life at the expense of me and my son, then he will surely destroy me and my children as well, in accordance with God’s will.
verses.17: And your wife shall say, “May the words of my lord, the king, be pleasing to God. For just as God fills His vessels with goodness, so too may my lord, the king, listen to both good and evil words. And Jehovah, your God, will be with you.”
verses.18: And the king said to the woman, “Please, do not be afraid of me. I am asking you a few questions.” And the woman said, “Please, speak to me, my lord, the king.”
verses.19: And the king said, “Yovav will take control of everything in this matter.” The woman replied, “Oh king, your servant Yovav is a wicked man. He put all these words into your mouth, oh king.”
verses.20: In order to understand the meaning of these words, your servant Yoab has done this. And my Lord is wise, just as God is wise. He knows everything that happens on earth.
verses.21: And the king said to Joab, “Now, I have done this. Go back and take the boy with you, Absalom.”
verses.22: And Joab fell face down to the ground, bowed down, and blessed the king. He said, “Today, your servant knows that I have found favor in your eyes, oh king! You have done what your servant had requested.”
verses.23: And Joab stood up, went forth with his men, and brought Abshalom back to Jerusalem.
verses.24: And the king said, “Let him go into his house, but let his face not be seen.” So Abshalom went into his house, and the king’s face was not seen.
verses.25: And in Abshalom, there would be no man who was handsome enough to be praised by everyone in Israel. From his feet to his head, there would be no one who could be praised at all.
verses.26: And when he shaved off his head, it would remain as long as the days that would pass until he could shave again. It was beautiful for him. Then he measured the length of his head in shekels, using the weight of the stone used for measuring.
verses.27: And Abshalom had six sons and one daughter. Her name was Tamar. She was a beautiful woman.
verses.28: And Abshalom stayed in Jerusalem for two years. But the king did not see him at all.
verses.29: And Abshalom sent him to Joab, so that he could be sent to the king. But he refused to go there. So Abshalom sent him again, but still he refused to go.
verses.30: And he said to his servants, “See, there’s a piece of wood at my hand. Go and light it on fire.” Then the servants of Abshalom burned that piece of wood with fire.
verses.31: And Joab stood up and went to Abishalom’s house. He said to him, “Why have your servants lit the fire that belongs to me?”
verses.32: And Abshalom said to Joab, “Look, I have sent you here with these words: ‘Go and present yourself before the king.’ What am I doing coming here with good news for me? I’m already there. Now, I will see the king’s face. And if there is any danger or threat to me…”
verses.33: Yoab went to the king and reported what had happened. He called for Abshalom’s presence. Abshalom came before the king and bowed his head in respect before the king. The king kissed Abshalom.
